trigger_description: No trigger identified. Pattern, intensity, size, and input location cannot be established from the inspected weights alone.
confidence_interpretation: Subjective, uncalibrated confidence in a tentative negative assessment; not a probability derived from behavioral testing.
assessment: No affirmative evidence of a backdoor found in static weight analysis; absence of a backdoor is not established.
edit_summary: No edits or ablated checkpoint produced: no sufficiently localized suspicious circuit was identified.
notes: Analyzed only the eight state_dict tensors in models/input/poisoned.pt. Checkpoint metadata values were not consulted. No datasets, reference checkpoint, image inputs, reconstructed network, forward passes, or training were used. Convolutional weight sharing does not identify an input location; fc1 spatial structure describes pooled feature coordinates, not a recovered pixel trigger. ReLU gates and max-pooling selections are input-dependent and were not evaluated. Distributed or low-magnitude learned backdoors can evade these static checks; normal-looking norms and spectra do not prove cleanliness. Trigger intensity and causal attack behavior remain unverified.
methods: Layer ranges, norms, sparsity, and finiteness
Singular values of flattened weight matrices
fc1 squared-weight concentration by channel and pooled spatial position
Inspection of conv1 kernels and selected high-norm/class-selective hidden units

evidence.candidate_review: fc1.46 had the largest incoming and outgoing norms, but only 6.41% of incoming squared-weight mass in its peak spatial cell and 7.65% in its peak channel, with positive outputs to classes 1, 7, and 2. Other reviewed units likewise showed distributed connections. These units are not designated backdoor units.
